nina: FYI finished the harbor-embed-v2 onboarding runs on the rerank+recall bench. posting concise results + next steps, ping @omar @sree for quick triage

omar: thanks. top-line numbers?

nina: baseline float32 recall@1/5/10 = 0.356 / 0.581 / 0.701. float16 close: 0.354 / 0.579 / 0.699. int8-pertensor naive = 0.332 / 0.554 / 0.673. int8-perchannel = 0.345 / 0.568 / 0.689. int5-perchannel (experimental) = 0.338 / 0.560 / 0.681. latency: float32 18.9ms/embed, float16 11.2ms, int8 6.9ms, int5 5.1ms.

sree: int5 interesting. how stable across seeds?

nina: std across 6 seeds: float32 recall@10 std 0.003, int8-perchannel 0.006, int5 0.009. silhouette: float32 0.26 -> int8 0.24 -> int5 0.20. ARI shows similar drop.

lucy: did you run per-language breakdown? we saw ja/regression patterns before.

nina: per-lang recall@10 deltas (int8-perchannel vs float32): en -0.006, de -0.007, ru -0.011, ja -0.038. int5 made ja worse (-0.055). short-query (<7 tokens) recall@10 delta vs float32: int8 -0.015, int5 -0.028. long queries (>160 tokens) unaffected.

omar: tokenization skew again for ja. any pre/postnorm experiments tried?

nina: yes ran three quick variants: (A) per-channel scales with 10k calibrations, (B) per-channel + per-dim clipping based on 99.9th percentile, (C) hybrid fp16 matmul + int8 KV cache. Results: A recall@10 = 0.689, B = 0.692, C = 0.695. C cut ja delta to -0.021.

sree: good. what's the index config? PQ/OPQ?

nina: index: HNSW M=12, ef_search=256, PQ off for main table. Ran OPQ+PQ(8) experiments: OPQ+PQ(8) on int8-perchannel -> recall@10 0.684 (index size -3.6x). OPQ applied on float32 gives small ARI boost but no recall win.

lucy: can you paste reproducible command?

nina: snippet below:

```
# harbor quick-eval
python eval_rerank_and_recall.py \
  --model harbor-embed-v2 \
  --quant MODE \
  --calib 10000 \
  --holdout rerank_recall_set.jsonl \
  --index hnsw --M 12 --ef_search 256 --dist cosine \
  --pq false --splits short:lt7,long:gt160,langs:en,de,ru,ja \
  --seeds 6
```

nnnina: MODE = float32 | float16 | int8-pt | int8-pc | int5-pc | hybrid-fp16-int8. All runs logged to artifacts.

ci-bot: nightly-eval job harbor-2026-04-15 completed \u2014 artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/harbor/6188884444/ (metrics.json, per_lang_table.csv, tsne_combined.png, norms_hist.png)

sree: any calibration-size sweep? small calib sets sometimes help ja tails.

nina: did a quick calib sweep for int8-perchannel: 1k->5k->10k->25k. recall@10 improved monotically: 0.681 -> 0.686 -> 0.689 -> 0.691. ja improved by ~0.009 absolute between 1k and 25k. int5 still noisy despite larger calib.

omar: what about small postnorm tweak? L2 normalize after quant + tiny bias?

nina: tried postnorm add-eps (0.01) then renormalize  recovered ~0.004 recall overall and helped short queries by ~0.006. combined with hybrid-fp16-int8 we'd be within product delta thresholds.

lucy: product asks: recommendation for Hosted default vs Dedicated opt-in?

omar: propose: Hosted: float16 default (lowest variance). Dedicated: int8-perchannel as opt-in with required calib >=10k and hybrid-fp16-int8 canary for sensitive langs. block int5 for now until seed variance acceptable. require per-lang recall delta alert at 1.5% absolute and short-query delta at 2.0% before promoted.

sree: please capture seed stds and per-lang small-golden set in PR. also include a short ablation: postnorm on/off, calib sizes.

nina: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/pull/1044  includes full tables, per-seed stats, scripts, and recommended rollout plan.

lucy: thanks. one more ask: add a small rerank-only golden set (few-shot) because downstream rerank sensitivity matters more than raw recall sometimes.

nina: adding rerank golden set now, will re-run the hybrid experiments and post back here.

eval-bot: label "onboard-review" added to PR #1044 by nina

ci-bot: coverage check: eval suite passed (smoke only)

nina: follow-ups: (1) hybrid microbench to quantify KV cache cost, (2) int8-perchannel calib sweep full run (started), (3) rerank golden set ablation. will post updates in this thread.

omar: thanks all, good detailed run. ping when calib sweep finishes.

nina: will do :rocket:
